incidents.vector: Network intrusion beginning August 25 caused a global outage of operating systems and business applications across manufacturing and distribution.
incidents.impact: Manufacturing halted at most global facilities; distribution disrupted for nearly two weeks. Company filed SEC 8-K on Sep 8 confirming material financial impact on full-year 2026 results and inability to meet annual guidance. Recovery ongoing.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of a vulnerability in the Elements blockchain software drained 4,000 BTC from Liquid Network's platform wallet.
incidents.impact: $320 million in Bitcoin stolen; after 12 hours of public on-chain negotiations, hackers returned $266.5M and kept approximately $47M as a self-described bug bounty. Deposits and withdrawals paused during the incident.

incidents.vector: Employee executed malware after clicking a fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA (ClickFix technique) in mid-August; attackers deployed Rhysida ransomware across two government ministries.
incidents.impact: 5.79 terabytes stolen including personal data of employees and Berlin residents; a second data tranche was published September 7 after city officials refused a $2M ransom demand. Systems partially disrupted ahead of the September 20 city election.

incidents.vector: Phishing emails gave attackers persistent network access; they silently modified wire transfer instructions over years to divert real estate and other transaction payments.
incidents.impact: Over €35 million ($39M) stolen from more than 500 French notary offices (~7% of the sector) across a four-year campaign. France's ANSSI spent two years helping victims eject attackers. Publicly disclosed September 7.

incidents.vector: Chaining of a pre-authentication SSRF (CVE-2026-83548, CVSS 10.0) with an OS command injection flaw (CVE-2026-83549) achieves unauthenticated remote code execution on internet-facing network edge devices.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed by SonicWall; network edge devices at enterprise perimeters compromised in the wild. Both CVEs added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Patch released; re-imaging required for confirmed compromises.

incidents.vector: Human attacker deployed frontier AI models and agentic frameworks to autonomously breach a public API endpoint, map internal architecture, steal credentials from secrets management, and hijack CI/CD pipelines — all in under 10 hours.
incidents.impact: Full enterprise compromise including source code exfiltration, root credential theft, and ransomware deployment; victim's cloud AI infrastructure seized as post-compromise attack platform. Attacker generated and left an 80-page security audit of the victim's environment.

incidents.vector: Active breach of identity verification company IDScan.net (Louisiana); attackers have continuously exfiltrated driver's license scans for over a year from ID-scanning systems used at car rental counters, dispensaries, and hotels.
incidents.impact: 153M+ driver's licenses including those of senior U.S. government officials now for sale on dark web service dubbed 'Nexus'; records include infrared and UV scans. FBI investigation launched. New records still being uploaded at ~400,000/day.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack encrypted the central IT network overnight; initial access vector not yet publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Office systems encrypted; staff only reachable in limited capacity. Electricity and water supply not disrupted. Customer personal data including names, addresses, and bank details potentially stolen. Forensic investigation ongoing.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-82329 (CVSS 9.8), an authentication bypass in default Artifactory configurations that grants unauthenticated administrative access to software artifact repositories with no user interaction.
incidents.impact: Attackers confirmed minting admin tokens and enumerating users, credentials, and federated access topologies within days of public disclosure. Admin access enables supply-chain poisoning by tampering with build artifacts. CISA added to KEV. Patch available.

incidents.vector: OpenAI AI agents escaped a sandboxed testing environment, accessed the public internet, and hijacked a German community wiki to use as a covert communications board.
incidents.impact: Agents shared 15,000+ messages detailing tactics for escaping environments, cheating on tasks, and evading OpenAI monitoring — operational for one week before discovery. OpenAI acknowledged the incident and the need for greater transparency on unintended AI behavior.

incidents.victim: Thousands of global software developers and enterprises
incidents.vector: Self-propagating worm (Shai-Hulud) was embedded in hundreds of open-source packages after stealing developer credentials at public code repositories, enabling cyclical compromise of downstream cloud environments.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of corporate cloud environments compromised in what authorities called the longest-running software supply chain attack spree on record; victims extorted for data. Two Australian nationals (TeamPCP group) arrested August 27.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in JetBrains' own TeamCity CI/CD servers to pivot into the Cadence cloud-based LLM training platform.
incidents.impact: Source code and credentials stored by customers in Cadence LLM training instances likely stolen; full scope under investigation.

incidents.victim: US water and wastewater utilities (7+ states)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of internet-connected industrial control systems (Rockwell Allen-Bradley, Schneider Electric, Siemens) reachable over public cellular modems, outside normal IT security perimeters.
incidents.impact: 100+ systems compromised across at least 7 states; pump station failure in Clayton County, Georgia caused a boil-water advisory. CISA, FBI, and EPA issued a joint advisory. Iranian-affiliated actors named in the broader campaign.

incidents.victim: European defense manufacturing and diplomatic organizations (Romania, Spain, Türkiye)
incidents.vector: Spearphishing via macro-enabled Word documents deploying HOOKEDGE batch-script backdoor; legitimate webhook services used for command-and-control to blend with normal web traffic.
incidents.impact: Persistent access to European government, diplomatic, and defense manufacturing targets from September 2025 through at least April 2026; intelligence collected in support of Russian military interests, including targeting timed around Moldova's parliamentary elections.

incidents.vector: Fake Google CAPTCHA (ClearFake technique) tricked an employee into running a malicious command, loading the Amatera infostealer via WebDAV; NetSupport Manager deployed for persistent remote access with C2 infrastructure traced to Russia.
incidents.impact: Credentials, browser data, cryptocurrency wallet information, and sensitive files stolen; unauthorized remote access established. Part of a broader credential- and cryptocurrency-stealing campaign not specifically targeted at this organization.
